newsitem.title: USA: New Hampshire teen-ager guilty of murder.
newsitem.headline: New Hampshire teen-ager guilty of murder.

text.p: A New Hampshire jury on Wednesday found a Rochester teenager guilty of killing his parents and sentenced him to life in prison without parole.

After four days of deliberation, the jury convicted 18-year-old Robert Dingman on two counts of first-degree murder and one count of conspiracy to commit murder. New Hampshire state Judge Bruce Mohl immediately pronounced the sentence.
"You will spend the remainder of your life in prison -- a sentence wholly justified by the brutality of your acts," the judge said after pronouncing sentence.
Dingman, his face drained of all colour, stood staring straight ahead as the judge sentenced him. As he was led out of the courtroom in handcuffs, he bowed his head in his hands.

The trial pitted brother against brother. Robert and his 15-year-old brother Jeffrey were arrested on Feb. 9 after police found the bodies of their parents, Eve and Vince Dingman, wrapped in plastic in the attic of their modest home.
Prosecution witnesses testied that the parents died from wounds inflicted by nine .22 calibre bullets shot into their bodies on the afternoon of Feb. 6.
Jeffrey Dingman pleaded guilty to second-degree murder and agreed to testify against his older brother in exchange for a lesser sentence. He was sentenced to 18 to 30 years in prison.

During the 2-1/2 week trial prosecutors said Robert Dingman bragged to friends before the shootings that "jail is the life" where he could "get three squares (meals) a day" and "play plenty of hoop (basketball)."

His brother testified that Robert was angry with his parents for imposing a curfew on him after he received poor grades, adding that Robert was also upset when his parents failed to get him cellphone.
During closing arguments, Assistant Attorney General John Kacavas brandished the murder weapon and recalled Jeffrey's testimony for jurors saying:

"Imagine the fear, imagine the confusion. Imagine the bewilderment as she looked up to see her first-born son standing over her pointing this weapon at the middle of her forehead. Imagine what Eve Dingman must have felt like as that defendant said: 'Shut up bitch.'"
Robert's lawyer Caroline Smith, who did not put her client on the stand or call any defence witnesses, left the courtroom without speaking to reporters.
